reconcile.connective: Defenders argue the three lists name three distinct men who merely share the tribal name Sheba, the same name attaching to different lineages settled in overlapping Arabian regions.

discrepancy.connective: The objection is pressed by Steve Wells, who lists Genesis 10:7, 25:3, and 10:28 side by side and asks plainly which man fathered Sheba, treating the three answers as mutually exclusive.

skeptic.name: Steve Wells
skeptic.work: The Skeptic's Annotated Bible, "Who was Sheba's father?" (skepticsannotatedbible.com/contra/sheba.html)
skeptic.attribution: Steve Wells, The Skeptic's Annotated Bible (online; print ed. 2013)

excerpts.excerpt_text: There seem to be three different people of this name mentioned in this chapter, and a fourth in Gen 25:3.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly and minimally states the canonical harmonization: the Shebas are distinct persons who share a name, not one man with conflicting fathers.

excerpts.excerpt_text: Sheba: the Sabaeans, with the capital Saba or Mareb, Mariaba regia (Plin.), whose connection with the Cushite (Gen 10:7) and Abrahamite Sabaeans (Gen 25:3) is quite in obscurity.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Names the three Shebas as separate lineages (Joktanite here, plus Cushite 10:7 and Abrahamite 25:3), treating them as distinct peoples sharing a name even while granting their interrelation is obscure.

excerpts.excerpt_text: Abraham's descendants probably settled in these regions and became identified by their names, along with people of other lineage.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Supplies the mechanism for the shared name: Abrahamic settlers took on the names of regions already occupied by other-lineage peoples, so one tribal name spans separate genealogies.

pd_work.resource: Adam Clarke, Commentary on the Bible (1832), on Genesis 10:7
pd_work.author: Adam Clarke
pd_work.note: Clarke treats this passage directly, distinguishing three (indeed four) different men named Sheba across Genesis 10 and 25 rather than one figure with conflicting fathers.
